title: reduce gpu memory and workspace: activation-checkpointing, scratch-buffers, and arena tuning
author: Priya Shah
ci_status: pass (first run flaky nvprof test, rerun fixed)
description: Motivation: reduce peak GPU memory and transient workspace usage during inference for long-context and high-batch workloads. This PR introduces a set of coordinated changes across the serving runtime: 1) conservative default arena sizes and more aggressive arena reclamation heuristics, 2) per-layer activation checkpointing option for decoder-only models to trade compute for memory during long sequences, 3) shrink-and-reuse scratch buffer sizing to avoid per-request over-allocation, 4) minor kernel selection tweaks to prefer memory-efficient kernels on constrained devices, and 5) scheduler adjustments so continuous-batching reclaims KV-cache transient buffers sooner. The changes are split into small, reviewable commits and aim to preserve latency SLAs while lowering out-of-memory rates and average memory footprints. See linked Linear tickets for perf targets and regression criteria.
commits: tune(cuda_allocator): reduce default arena sizes and add reclamation pass
feat(runtime): per-layer activation checkpointing flag with warmup heuristic
perf(scratch): add shrink-and-reuse scratch buffer pool for inference paths
opt(kernels): prefer mem-efficient kernel variants for small-GPU profiles
sched(batch): reclaim transient KV cache buffers earlier in continuous batching
test: add regression tests for long-context memory usage
docs: runtime flags and troubleshooting notes
